title: Eschatology
english: The world and judgment will be given to him because the sun and moon will be darkened, and the heavens will be rolled up.
Before Christ's presence, the Antichrist will come, killing many, and then will be a time of tribulation.

With him and how Christ, the sign of Christ will be revealed, and the kingdom will not have an end. For from before the ages the Son was born, as it is written, 'From the womb before the dawn I begot you' (Psalm 89:3).

Similarly, Wisdom says, 'Before the age I was founded in the beginning, before the earth was made and before the depths, and before the springs of water came forth, and before the mountains were established, before all hills I was born' (Wisdom of Solomon 1:25). And David again says in the 72nd psalm, 'He will endure with the sun and before the moon for generations of generations' (Psalm 72:5).
He was with the Father, as Moses says in the creation of the world, 'Let us make man in our image and according to our likeness' (Genesis 1:26).
Wisdom says, 'When he prepared the heaven, I was with him,' and 'I saw your works, being present when you made the world,' indicating that the Son was indeed born before the ages.

The Lord God, who made the heaven and established it, who strengthened the earth and what is in it, and gives breath to the people on it and to those who walk on it, as He says, 'I, the Lord God, called you and gave you as a covenant to the nation, as a light to the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, to bring out the prisoners from bondage, and those sitting in darkness from the prison house' (Isaiah 42:6-7).
The Lord will send His angel before His face, and he will look at the way, as Malachi says, 'Behold, I send my angel before your face, and he will look at the way' (Malachi 3:1).
And again: 'He sent me to preach the gospel to the poor' (Isaiah 61:1).
David, in the 42nd psalm, says that He sent His word and healed them (Psalm 42:4).
Jacob prophesied that a ruler will not fail from Judah and a leader from his loins until what is to be comes, and he is the expectation of the nations (Genesis 49:10).

Moses prophesied that the Lord God will raise up a prophet for you from your brothers like me, and you will listen to him in all things (Deuteronomy 18:15); and it will be that whoever does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed forever (Deuteronomy 18:19).
Hosea says, 'We will find him like the morning dawn, and he will come like the early and late rain to the earth' (Hosea 6:3).
Amos says, 'On that day, he will raise up the fallen tent of David and rebuild what has been destroyed' (Amos 9:11).
Micah says, 'From the mountains of Zion, the law will go out, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem' (Micah 4:2).
Joel says, 'The Lord will shout from Zion and give his voice from Jerusalem' (Joel 2:16).
He also says, 'You will know that the Lord our God is, and he will dwell on his holy mountain' (Joel 3:17).
Furthermore, the Lord will dwell in Zion, as Obadiah says, 'In Mount Zion there will be salvation; for the day of the Lord is near upon all nations' (Obadiah 1:17).
The prophet Jonah will suffice as a type of death (Jonah).
Nahum declares that the Lord is good to those who wait for Him, and the Lord says He is coming upon them (Nahum 1:7).
Habakkuk says that the one who is coming will come and not delay (Habakkuk 2:3).
Zephaniah says, 'Rejoice, daughter of Zion, for the Lord has removed your injustices; the Lord will reign in your midst' (Zephaniah 3:14-15).
The Lord will dwell in the midst of Zion, and Haggai says the Lord is with them, as he says, 'I am with you, says the Lord' (Haggai 2:4).

Zechariah also says, 'Rejoice, daughter of Zion, for I am coming and will dwell in your midst' (Zechariah 8:3), and the Lord says He will return to Zion and dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and Jerusalem will be called the city of truth (Zechariah 8:8).

title: Messianic Prophecy
english: Malachi says, 'I am a great king,' says the Lord, the ruler of all, and my name shall be renowned among the nations (Malachi 3:2). He will come suddenly to his temple, says the Lord God, whom you desire, and the angel of the covenant, whom you seek (Malachi 3:1). Behold, he comes, says the Lord; his name is the sun of righteousness, and healing in his wings (Malachi 4:2). The sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear him (Malachi 4:2). Isaiah says, 'In those last days the mountain of the Lord and the house of God will be prominent at the summit of the mountains; the law will go out from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem' (Isaiah 2:3). The Lord himself will come for anointing with the elders of the people (Isaiah 60:1). And again, on that day God will shine with glory upon the earth (Isaiah 60:1).

A rod will come from the root of Jesse, and a flower will rise from the root, and the spirit of God will rest upon him: a spirit of wisdom, a spirit of understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and reverence; and the spirit of the fear of God will fill him (Isaiah 11:1-3). And again, you will see a king with glory (Isaiah 60:1). A voice cries in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, make straight the paths of God our Lord' (Matthew 3:3). Behold, the Lord comes with strength (Isaiah 60:1). The root of Jesse will arise to rule the nations, and the nations will hope in him (Isaiah 11:10).

In you they will pray, because God is in you, and they will say, 'There is no God except you; for you are God, and we did not know' (Malachi 3:7). Jeremiah says, 'Christ the Lord is the Spirit before our face' (Jeremiah 31:31). 'Remember me, Lord, and visit me; and rescue me from those pursuing me' (Jeremiah 31:30). Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, 'and I will raise up for David a righteous branch, and a king will reign, and he will understand, and he will do judgment and righteousness upon the earth' (Jeremiah 33:15). In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell confidently upon him (Jeremiah 33:16). And this is the name by which he will be called, Josedeck, and he is among the prophets (Jeremiah 33:15).

And again, they will know the prophet whom the Lord sent to them in faith (Jeremiah 31:34). And again, 'Pray to me and I will listen to you; seek and you will find me, if you seek me with all your heart, and I will appear to you' (Jeremiah 29:13). And again, the Lord is coming to his holy mountain (Isaiah 52:8). And Ezekiel says, 'The likeness of their faces, the four: a face of a man, and a face of a lion, and a face of a calf, and a face of an eagle' (Ezekiel 1:10). And again, 'I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an eternal covenant; and you will remember your way' (Ezekiel 16:60). And again, 'From my holy mountain, upon a high mountain, says the Lord, there all the house of Israel will serve me until the end' (Ezekiel 37:27). And again, 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will seek my sheep and I will visit them, just as a shepherd seeks his flock' (Ezekiel 34:11).

And again, they will know that I am the Lord their God when I appear to them among the nations (Ezekiel 37:28). And Balaam says, 'A man will come out of the seed of Israel, and he will rule many nations' (Numbers 24:17). And again, 'A star will rise out of Jacob, and a man will rise out of Israel, and he will crush the strong ones of Moab' (Numbers 24:17). And Daniel says, 'Until Christ the leader, seven weeks and sixty-two weeks' (Daniel 9:25). And David says, 'When the Lord returns the captivity of his people, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad' (Psalm 126:1).

And again, he set his tabernacle in the sun; and he will come out like a bridegroom from his chamber, and will rejoice like a giant to run the way (Psalm 19:4-6). His going out is from the end of heaven, and his circuit is to the end of heaven (Psalm 19:6). And again, 'Make your face shine upon your servant' (Psalm 110:3). And again, 'He bowed the heavens and came down' (Psalm 18:9). And again, 'The God of gods will be seen in Zion' (Psalm 68:35). And again, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; God is the Lord and he has appeared to us' (Psalm 118:26). And again, the angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him and will deliver them (Malachi 3:3). And again, he will come down like rain upon the mown grass (Malachi 3:1). And again, the Lord is near to those who are brokenhearted (Psalm 34:18). And again, make his face shine upon…

title: Incarnation
english: We ask that God have mercy on us and dwell among humans, so that all people can see His salvation.
As Solomon said, if God truly dwells with humans.
This is the God who became human, as Jeremiah proclaimed, and there is no other like Him.
He gave knowledge to Jacob and Israel, and David declared that truth arose from the earth, and a man was born, founded by God Himself.
The prophets also spoke of God's presence among humans, with Hosea saying that his flesh is from them, and Isaiah stating that God is with us, and that He was found by those who did not seek Him.
In Him, people will pray, because He is the one true God, and David affirmed that the Lord's offspring will remain forever, and that God swore to David and will not revoke His promise.

The Lord will set His offspring on the throne, and their throne will endure like the heavens, as Isaiah also said: 'I will put his kingdom on David's throne to establish and take hold in righteousness and judgment.' (Isaiah 9:6-7)

As Jeremiah prophesied, the days are coming when God will raise up a righteous branch for David, and he will reign as king, demonstrating his understanding and wisdom in judgment and righteousness on the earth. (Jeremiah 23:5-6)
During his reign, Israel and Judah will be saved and will dwell in safety.
The prophet Isaiah also foretold the birth of Christ, saying that a virgin would conceive and bear a son, and his name would be called Emmanuel, which means 'God with us'. (Isaiah 7:14)

Furthermore, Ezekiel described a vision in which the Lord said to him, 'Son of man, this gate will be closed, and no one will pass through it, except the Lord God alone, who will enter and sit, and then go out and close the doors behind him, and the gate will remain closed forever.' (Ezekiel 44:1-3)
In a similar vein, Job lamented, 'Why did you not close the doors of my mother's womb for me?' (Job 3:10)
Meanwhile, Isaiah proclaimed, 'Before the one in labor gives birth, before the pains of labor come, she has escaped and given birth to a male.' (Isaiah 66:7)

The anointing of Christ is also a significant theme, as David said, 'Therefore, God anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions,' (Psalm 45:7) and Isaiah declared, 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me.' (Isaiah 61:1)
Finally, Jeremiah expressed his sorrow, saying, 'Woe is me, mother.' (Jeremiah 4:31; 15:20)
David cried out to God, 'My God, my God, attend to me.' (Psalm 22:1)
For it is God who drew me out of my mother's womb and placed me in the care of my parents.
From the moment of my birth, I was cast upon God, and he has been my rock and my salvation.
The prophet Daniel saw a vision of a stone cut without hands, which would strike the image of worldly power and bring about a new era of peace and righteousness. (Daniel 2:34-35)
The stone, as Isaiah foretold, would be a stone of stumbling in Zion, a rock of offense to those who refuse to believe. (Isaiah 8:14)
Yet, for those who put their faith in God, this stone would be a source of strength and comfort.
Zechariah saw a vision of this stone, with seven eyes looking out upon all the earth. (Zechariah 3:9; 4:10)
The birth of Jesus, as foretold by Isaiah, would be a moment of great joy and celebration, for a child is born to us, a son is given to us, and his government would be upon his shoulder. (Isaiah 9:6)
The magi, as David prophesied, would come to worship him, bringing gifts.
